subject: Intermittent SNAT imbalance + MTU stalls during Fairview private cutover
messages:
From: Adam Turner <adam.turner@fairview-health.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Fairview NOC <noc@fairview-health.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent timeouts after private cutover

Hi Rachel,

We cut over the private link for the Fairview VPC last night and are seeing intermittent TCP stalls / retransmits affecting our API traffic to your private frontdoor. Symptoms: 5-10% of connections see long stalls (~6-12s) on first few hundred bytes, then recover. We see packet reordering and occasional SYN retries.

Quick notes:
- Traffic is egressing through the secondary NIC on the appliance (eth1).
- MTU counters on our edge show fragmentation events but no ICMP blackhole logs.
- We captured a short tcpdump during a hit (attached).

Can you triage? This is impacting production traffic and we'd like a hotfix path.

Attachments: fairview_cutover_capture_0514.pcap (pcap, ~2.3MB)

Thanks,
Adam Turner
Network Engineering Lead
Fairview Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Adam Turner <adam.turner@fairview-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts after private cutover

Thanks Adam — sorry you're seeing this. I'm pulling Marissa and Karthik in for network-level triage.

Please do the following while we look:
- Run an MTR/TRACE from your edge to the private frontdoor IP and paste results.
- Confirm exact ephemeral port range on your firewall (are you NAT-ing to a small pool?).
- If you can, run iperf3 for short bursts to try and reproduce microbursts.

Marissa / Karthik — attaching the pcap from Fairview. Initial hypothesis: SNAT imbalance across our frontdoor cluster + MTU-related fragmentation/clamping on the secondary NIC could cause reordering and TCP stalls. Also want to validate SG/stateful timeouts on the Private connector.

Attachments: quick-triage-checklist.md

I'll keep this high priority — please update with any immediate mitigations (temporary SNAT pool expansion, MSS clamp) and we'll coordinate rollback windows if needed.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Adam Turner <adam.turner@fairview-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts after private cutover

Hi all — dug into the capture and a few frontdoor nodes. Summary and suggested mitigations below.

What I see:
- Multiple flows from Fairview are being SNATed by different frontdoor hosts with uneven ephemeral port distribution. Some nodes are at >85% of ephemeral port allocation under short bursts. That can cause port reuse and spurious RSTs from intermediate NATs.
- The capture shows out-of-order sequence numbers and duplicated ACKs consistent with asymmetric path / reordering.
- Edge counters show small fragments and IP reassembly attempts; MTU looks like 1500 on the wire but we see a middlebox clamping MSS down to 1400 intermittently (likely a load-balancer or firewall rule).
- Security group on the private connector is restricting source ephemeral ranges (looks like someone limited to 32768-49151) while our SNAT pool was smaller than expected (we had a mis-apply during the cutover).

Immediate mitigations I applied (non-disruptive):
- Expanded SNAT pool on the affected frontdoor ASG by +40% (temporary).
- Enabled per-flow affinity on SNAT to reduce cross-host port juggling for current connections.
- Applied MSS clamp (1400) on egress path for traffic from Fairview as a stopgap.

Results so far: retransmits/retries dropped from ~6% to ~1.2% in the synthetic tests Adam ran back-to-back. Adam — can you confirm your production traces after these changes?

Longer-term actions:
- Normalize ephemeral port ranges with Fairview and coordinate firewall rules so SNAT pool + ephemeral range covers peak concurrency.
- Increase SNAT pool size and ensure autoscaling adds SNAT capacity before cutovers.
- Add a pre-cutover validation step to check per-host SNAT saturation and MSS clamping detection.

Attachments: snat_table_snapshot_0514.txt, mss-clamp-playbook.md

If this looks stable Adam, we'd like to schedule a brief postmortem tomorrow and then follow with a remediation rollout (non-peak). If not, we have a rollback plan to revert the cutover in the next 30 minutes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts after private cutover

Marissa / Rachel — thanks for the quick turnaround.

We validated this morning after your SNAT pool expansion + MSS clamp. Production error rate on the API endpoints dropped from ~5% to ~0.7% over the morning window. We still see a small number of retries during very short bursts (~0.5% of connections) but nothing close to the impact we saw overnight.

Next asks:
- Can you provide the permanent rollout plan for increasing SNAT capacity and ensuring autoscale pre-warms during cutovers?
- We'll need a follow-up joint validation run before the final cutover (preferably Wed 05/19 02:00-05:00 UTC).
- Please open a Jira with the remediation steps we discussed and include runbooks so our NOC can follow in future.

I've attached a short post-check tcpdump and a link to a trace we saved.

Attachments: fairview_postcheck_0515.pcap

Thanks again — we'll stand by for the remediation timeline.

Adam Turner
Network Engineering Lead
Fairview Health
